extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Change-summary guidance and updated instructions from the MPEP Ninth Edition Revision 01.2024 describing substantive and procedural examination standards across multiple chapters (e.g., novelty/obviousness, claim construction, filings, appeals, design/plant patents, international/national-phase practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for joint or sole inventor and AIA definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to more clearly articulate guidance when there is a joint inventor or sole inventor and to reflect AIA definitions of applicant and inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies application of inventor-related rules under AIA definitions, including who qualifies as an inventor or applicant for purposes across sections (affects prior possession, attribution, copending application rejections, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: References have a 'prior art date'
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that references have a 'prior art date' (and added this language in the preamble and subsections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should treat references as having a discrete prior art date for analyses (e.g., anticipation, obviousness, effective dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's prior possession
rubrics_metrics.description: Added 'the inventor's' before 'prior possession' to clarify ownership of prior possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering prior possession as a basis to antedate references or rebut prior art, the prior possession must be that of the inventor (i.e., the inventor's prior possession matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Person of ordinary skill terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaced 'skilled' with 'of ordinary skill' and corrected related citations (e.g., In re Schaub).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the phrase 'person of ordinary skill in the art' consistently when discussing skill-level-based analyses (e.g., obviousness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective filing date is of the claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that the effective filing date is of 'the claimed invention' in the application or patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining priority and effective dates, focus on the claimed invention(s) — the effective date pertains to the claims for which entitlement is asserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of production for commercial success evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Title revised to 'BURDEN OF PRODUCTION FOR EVIDENCE OF COMMERCIAL SUCCESS AND NEXUS' and guidance clarified on the burden of production for evidence of commercial success by removing discussion of nexus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies examiner/applicant burdens regarding commercial success evidence: who must produce what evidence and how nexus should be treated in that burden analysis (see In re Huang and other cited cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who bears burden of establishing nexus
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified who bears the burden of establishing a nexus and added a citation to In re Huang.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which party (applicant/patentee) must establish the nexus between claimed features and commercial success for secondary considerations to be accorded weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution language for secondary considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaced 'DERIVED FROM' with 'ATTRIBUTABLE TO' and replaced 'directly derived from' with 'a result of' in subsection I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use refined attribution language when assessing whether secondary considerations (e.g., commercial success) are attributable to the claimed invention rather than external factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments must be described as by applicant (not 'attorney arguments')
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised title and phrasing: replace 'ATTORNEY ARGUMENTS'/'The arguments of counsel' with 'ARGUMENTS BY APPLICANT'/'Arguments presented by the applicant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive arguments are characterized as presented by the applicant (rather than by counsel), which clarifies who is the source of arguments and may affect evidentiary consideration and signature/authorization requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration signature requirements under 37 CFR 1.33(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Added 'The statement must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b).' (for subsections I.B and III).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits and declarations submitted under relevant sections must strictly comply with the signature requirements of 37 CFR 1.33(b); examiners should check for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should file 37 CFR 1.130 affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified who should file the affidavit (and added cross reference to MPEP § 2155.05).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance identifies proper filers and cross-references procedural rules for attribution/prior public disclosure exceptions for 37 CFR 1.130 filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace 'domestic reference' with 'U.S. patent or patent application publication'
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaced 'domestic reference' with 'U.S. patent or patent application publication.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise statutory/regulatory categories when referring to U.S. patent literature as prior art for examination purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify prior art date of a reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to clarify that the reference has a prior art date in multiple subsections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should explicitly determine and state the prior art date for references relied upon in rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and guidance inclusion for recent Federal Circuit cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Added citations and discussions of recent Federal Circuit decisions (e.g., EmeraChem, Volvo Penta, UCB v. Actavis, Yita v. MacNeil, Campbell Soup v. Gamon, Amgen v. Amneal, etc.) across multiple sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate legal precedent into examination guidance where the cited cases affect interpretation of statutes, burden allocations, claim construction, secondary considerations, or other substantive examiner analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party preissuance submissions: concise descriptions may include arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that a concise explanation for a protest under § 1.291(c)(2) allows for arguments against patentability, aligning with AIA preissuance submission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions may include concise explanations and arguments against patentability; follow updated web-based filing and fee instructions (including small entity fee handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission web interface and processing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated website addresses and instructions for filing a third-party submission via the dedicated web-based interface; clarified that applicant papers filed via that interface will not be entered into the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions should be filed using the specified USPTO interface; applicants must use registered EFS/Patent Center accounts to file papers in their own applications — submissions via the third-party interface will not enter the applicant's file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity fee handling for third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated instructions and fee amounts for paying the small entity fee when submitting a third-party submission via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the updated fee schedule and payment instructions when a third-party elects small entity status for fees associated with preissuance submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must bring prior art search up-to-date prior to allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that an examiner is expected to bring a prior art search up-to-date prior to allowance on an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should perform or update searches for intervening art before allowing claims to ensure allowance is based on current prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of new rejections for appealed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner proposes a new rejection for an appealed claim as to which the examiner was reversed, the proposed rejection must be submitted to the TC or CRU Director unless an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects appellant rights by requiring supervisory review before issuing new rejections on claims recently reversed by the Board, except in specified exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require title amendment if unsatisfactory
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that if a satisfactory title is not supplied by the applicant, the examiner may require a change to the title on or after allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may request or make title changes to ensure the title corresponds to the claimed invention, subject to constraints and exceptions (e.g., Office-established title situations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant comments on reasons for allowance deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that any comments filed by applicant on the examiner’s statement of reasons for allowance must be filed no later than payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant feedback on reasons for allowance has a firm deadline (issue fee payment); examiners should treat late comments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic issuance and printed-patent status
rubrics_metrics.description: Added cross references indicating electronically issued patents are considered printed patents (37 CFR 1.9(k)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat electronically issued patents as printed patents for rules and references that depend on 'printed patent' status (affects prior art analyses, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture / surrendered subject matter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that, in the context of recapture case law, claims are considered canceled if they were replaced by other claims that are more specific than the canceled claims in at least one aspect in order to overcome a rejection; added examples, definitions (SGL), flowchart, and related citations (In re McDonald, In re Youman, In re Mostafazadeh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a stepwise framework for analyzing recapture: identify canceled claims, determine whether reissue claims broaden in ways that relate to surrendered subject matter, and apply situational examples; use revised flowchart and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph and procedure updates for reissue/reissue cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised form paragraphs and example language for cross-referencing multiple reissue applications and requesting supplemental oaths/declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use updated form paragraphs and submission procedures for reissue practice, including how to reference multiple reissue applications resulting from a single patent and how to request supplemental oaths/declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent representation and electronic images guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Added a new 'Design Patent Practitioner Bar' section and incorporated Supplemental Guidance for Examination of Design Patent Applications Related to Computer-Generated Electronic Images, including icons and GUIs; clarified who may represent, how to depict color in black-and-white line drawings, and cross references for evaluating secondary considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent practitioners and patent practitioners admitted under specified CFR sections may represent applicants; examiners should apply the supplemental guidance and examples when examining electronic images, icons, and GUIs and follow cross-references for secondary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent examination clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to add examples of asexual reproduction means (apomictic seeds, bulbs, division, etc.), incorporate plain meaning of 'plant,' reiterate plant patent is limited to one plant/genome and that invention in a plant is a two-step process; clarified inventor qualification and acceptable drawing types (watercolor renderings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine plant patent applications with these substantive limits in mind; consider examples of asexual reproduction, genome uniqueness, and acceptable drawings when assessing compliance and inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO Standard ST.26 and sequence listing for national phase applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated and clarified overall guidance on WIPO Standard ST.26 and when sequence listings must comply with PCT Administrative Instructions (for international applications with filing date on/after July 1, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For national phase entries, ensure sequence listings are provided as separate parts of the description and comply with ST.26 where applicable; follow updated editor notes that reproduced rules apply to national phase applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage payment/fee application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Added paragraph clarifying that when a payment of fees in a national stage application lacks sufficient specification for which fees are to be applied, the Office will apply payment first to the basic national fee unless the applicant specified otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicants underpay or misallocate payments in national stage filings, the Office will first apply funds to the basic national fee; examiners/clerks should follow this application order unless explicit instructions are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention applies in national stage and examiner may make lack of unity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that unity of invention analysis is applicable in national stage applications submitted under 35 U.S.C. 371 and that the examiner may make a lack of unity requirement even if no such requirement was made by the ISA or IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should perform unity/lack-of-unity analyses for national stage entries and may require restriction/clarification consistent with 37 CFR and MPEP cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction timing and evidence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaced 'the time the invention was made' with 'the relevant time' and emphasized that it is not necessary to identify a single statutory category into which a claim falls so long as it is clear the claim falls into at least one statutory category; included numerous case law citations (Phillips, Salazar, Sisvel, Malvern Panalytical, Actelion, CCS Fitness, Apple v. Corephotonics, Biogen, United Therapeutics, Amgen, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'relevant time' for claim construction analyses, consult cited case law for rules on consulting extrinsic evidence and claim meaning, and apply the flexible statutory-category approach when assessing claim eligibility/subject matter classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.14(a) copending application rejection basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that 37 CFR 1.14(a) applies to all pending U.S. patent applications and that rejections may be made when copending applications have 'at least one' inventor in common or differ by at least one 'joint' inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may make rejections based on copending applications under 1.14(a) where inventor overlap exists (including joint inventors), and should ensure appropriate factual comparison and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publications and Wayback Machine guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaced 'Prior art disclosures' with 'Electronic publications' in II.B and clarified guidance regarding the Wayback Machine® in II.E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on online materials, treat them as 'electronic publications' and follow provided guidance on how to evaluate archived captures (e.g., Wayback Machine) as prior art and how to determine dates and reliability.
